title: Randomized Trial of Verubecestat for Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer’s Disease
venue: The New England journal of medicine

one_line: A randomized trial of the BACE-1 inhibitor verubecestat in patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease was terminated early due to futility, failing to reduce cognitive or functional decline despite lowering cerebrospinal fluid amyloid-beta levels.
summary: This document reports the findings of a 78-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating verubecestat, an oral BACE-1 inhibitor, in 1,958 patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. Patients received either 12 mg or 40 mg of verubecestat daily or a matching placebo. The trial was terminated early for futility 50 months after onset. Results indicated no significant differences between the verubecestat and placebo groups in the coprimary outcomes of cognitive (ADAS-cog) and functional (ADCS-ADL) decline. While the drug successfully lowered Aβ levels in the cerebrospinal fluid and modestly reduced brain amyloid load, it was associated with an increased incidence of adverse events, including falls, rash, sleep disturbances, suicidal ideation, and weight loss. The findings suggest that targeting amyloid production with a BACE-1 inhibitor may not be effective once mild-to-moderate clinical symptoms of Alzheimer's disease have emerged.

key_claims.claim: Verubecestat does not reduce cognitive or functional decline in patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
key_claims.evidence: The estimated mean change from baseline to week 78 in the ADAS-cog score was 7.9 in the 12-mg group, 8.0 in the 40-mg group, and 7.7 in the placebo group (P=0.63 and P=0.46). The ADCS-ADL score changes were -8.4, -8.2, and -8.9 respectively (P=0.49 and P=0.32).

key_claims.claim: Verubecestat successfully reduces Aβ production and modestly reduces brain amyloid load.
key_claims.evidence: Cerebrospinal fluid concentrations of Aβ-40 were reduced by 71.1-80.6%, and Aβ-42 by 62.7-76.4%. The mean standardized uptake value ratio for PET amyloid load in the 40-mg group decreased from 0.87 at baseline to 0.83 at week 78.

key_claims.claim: Verubecestat is associated with higher rates of adverse events compared to placebo.
key_claims.evidence: Adverse events leading to discontinuation occurred in 9.4% (40-mg), 8.3% (12-mg), and 5.8% (placebo) of patients. Higher rates of falls, rash, sleep disturbance, decreased weight, and suicidal ideation were observed in treatment groups compared to placebo.

methods.population: Patients aged 55 to 85 years with a clinical diagnosis of mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease and an MMSE score of 15 to 26

funding_and_conflicts: Funded by Merck. Conflicts of interest are stated to be available in disclosure forms at NEJM.org but are not detailed in the text.
limitations: Lack of requirement for the presence of an amyloid biomarker at screening, potentially allowing inclusion of patients with nonamyloid-related dementia.
Uncontrolled selection of patients for the biomarker substudies, which may have introduced bias.
